title: Electric Propulsion
description: An ion engine does not burn anything: it ionises a heavy gas (xenon, here freed from a clathrate) and pulls the ions out through charged grids. The exhaust leaves ten times faster than any flame, but the thrust is a breath, so an ion stage takes months to do what a chemical one does in minutes. Dawn and DS1 flew this way. Unlocks the Ion Thruster Grid.

puzzle.goal: An ion of charge q and mass m falls through a potential difference V between the grids. Write the speed v it leaves with.
puzzle.name: Ion exhaust
puzzle.ask: Find v in km/s for a xenon ion (q = 1.602e-19 C, m = 2.18e-25 kg) through V = @{V} V (give m/s ÷ 1000).
puzzle.method: The field does work qV on the ion; all of it becomes kinetic energy, ½mv².
